# Ontology agentic data quality note v0

## source metadata - source_title: `Ontology and agentic AI data quality discussion` - source_author: `unknown video speaker` - source_type: `external transcript text` - source_capture_date: `2026-04-23` - source_note_ki

## why this source matters This source matters because it argues that agentic systems need structured and curated data foundations, not just more agent loops. It overlaps with our current space around: - hallucination li

## core claim The source argues that an agent ecosystem built on LLMs alone remains unstable because hallucination and poor data quality remain unresolved. Its proposed answer is not "more prompting" but stronger structu
### 2. ontology is dynamic, not static The source pushes toward an active ontology model where entities, relations, and updates remain live instead of frozen.

### 3. data quality is a bottleneck Even a strong structural model fails if: - source data is incomplete - authority or reference quality is weak - public data looks complete but is actually thin or broken
### 4. structure can reduce downstream burden If the data layer is better organized, downstream search, response, and cost pressure can drop.

## relevance to our current space This is not a direct architecture replacement. It is useful because it reinforces several active pressures in our space: - source quality before promotion - structure before strong opera

## bounded judgment Current bounded judgment: - useful as a data quality and relation-structure reference - relevant for recurrence around structure, maintenance, and source quality pressure - not a direct order to build
